about: Fifth held-out intent set. Written to probe a failure class found by a screenshot rather than by any evaluation: asked 'Can I work from my house a few days a week?', the app filed a five-day casual leave application. The intent classifier routed a policy question to applyLeave. Scored on the 36 retrieval paraphrases in policy_queries.json -- 36 policy questions the intent work had never looked at -- the shipping classifier routed 14 of them to a leave action. This file exists so the fix is measured on cases written before it, in the same order set 4 was.
what_it_probes: Policy questions about non-leave topics, phrased in the first person and in the register a chat box actually produces. That is the gap: the intent training set is overwhelmingly leave-centric, so the classifier learned that a first-person sentence containing a day, a time or a duration is a leave action. Attendance, payroll, IT, expenses, grievance, medical and exit questions all carry those words and are not requests for anything.
why_this_matters_more_than_an_accuracy_p: A misroute here is not a slightly worse answer, it is the wrong action. policyQuestion answers a question; applyLeave attempts to file leave against a real balance. The failure the app was rebuilt to prevent was fabricating a leave confirmation, and routing a policy question into applyLeave arrives at the same place by a different road.
honest_characterisation: This is a TARGETED REGRESSION SET, not a random sample of user input. It was written after the failure class was known, so a good score on it means the specific gap is closed and does not by itself mean the classifier generalises. Sets 3 and 4 remain the general measurement and are reported alongside it. It is balanced 12/12/12 on purpose: a set of policy questions alone could be passed by a classifier that answers policyQuestion to everything, which would break both leave features instead.
